title: Scaling Systems
hook: Ten clients was fine. Twenty almost broke me. Same business, just more of it.
statement: Your systems either scale as you grow or they break. Build them before volume forces you to.
explainer: If every new customer needs more of your personal time, growth just means more hours. Scalable systems let you serve more without working proportionally more.
sop: List your core processes: fulfillment, onboarding, support, hiring, invoicing.
For each, ask if your Effort rises one for one with Output.
Flag every process where your personal time is the limit.
Rebuild the flagged ones as templates, tools, or delegated workflows.
Test on paper at 2x volume and note where it strains.
equation_example: Output 100 customers, Effort 40 of your hours. 100 ÷ 40 = 2.5 customers per hour. Higher means each hour supports more as you grow. Lower means growth just eats more of your time.
question: Name one process that would break if you had ten times the customers next month.
closing_statement: Build so growth outpaces your own effort.
